mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% month-over-month in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods (HOUST > 0.5% MoM), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where both UNRATE declines and PAYEMS growth accelerates, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic regimes (characterized by high GDP growth and low unemployment), a rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals potential overheating and impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle periods with rising INDPRO, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior 3 months indicates improving labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation, prompting anticipated monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% month-over-month in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods (CPIAUCSL > 0.3% MoM), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS are rising, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-growth economic regimes (GDPC1 annualized growth > 3%), a rising housing market (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of high-growth periods with rising HOUST, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
